_design_note:
Rainbow, as far as this codebase implements it: Double DQN + n-step(5) + prioritized replay + a C51 distributional head, at a 10000-round budget. Four of Rainbow's six components; dueling and noisy nets are not implemented for a handcrafted-feature MLP and would each be new code.

The budget is the part with evidence behind it. The PER arm's learning curve on the loot-crate primary suite is behind R02_9 at every checkpoint and still climbing at 5000 rounds -- 15.52 at 4000 and 16.42 at 5000, where R02_9 had already flattened at 16.38 and 16.60 -- so prioritized sampling on this recipe learns roughly 1.7x slower per round rather than faster. A Rainbow arm at 5000 rounds would measure an undertrained agent. 10000 rounds is where the curve has room to finish.

An explanation this arm does NOT rest on: the first PER arm was read as training at 0.4x its declared step size, because its mean importance weight sat at 0.40 and its gradient norm at 0.486 against R02_9's 1.120. That reading is wrong and the measurement that kills it is the parameter norm -- PER reached 29.72 / 36.18 / 39.16 at rounds 1000 / 2500 / 5000 against R02_9's 29.19 / 35.79 / 38.63. The weights moved just as far. Adam divides by the running RMS of the gradient, so a uniform rescaling of the loss leaves the update almost unchanged, and it did. Sixth time on this line that an unmeasured mechanism has been wrong.

_predeclared_design_numbers.changed_factor: Three against R02_9: distributional head, prioritized sampling, and 10000 rounds instead of 5000. A submission candidate, not an ablation; if it wins, the credit is not divisible.
_predeclared_design_numbers.control: runs/rep_lr/ (R02_9, ten repeats, score 3.6371). The component arms are runs/rep_c51 (C51 alone), runs/rep_per (PER alone), runs/rep_budget (10000 rounds with the scalar head, t = -0.27).
_predeclared_design_numbers.cost: Measured: C51 is 482 us per gradient step against the scalar head's 259, and a 10000-round arm takes about 1.2 million of them. Training about 3.5 hours, evaluation about 35 minutes at checkpoint_every 500, repeats about 10 minutes.
_predeclared_design_numbers.falsification: Indistinguishable from R02_9 over ten repeats closes the Rainbow direction on the handcrafted line, and with it every algorithmic lever this codebase has.
_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction: Low. Every pairwise stack tried on this line so far has failed to compose: C51 at 7000 rounds lost both parents' best numbers (section 7.36), and the budget's effect on coins reverses sign under the distributional head. The one honest reason to run it is that PER has never been given the rounds its own curve says it needs, and Rainbow is the configuration that combination is named after.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reporting: All five training-seed distributions, coins_share and suicides beside every score, the learning curve, and the per-seed holdout numbers -- the submission is one model, not the pooled mean (section 7.37).
_predeclared_design_numbers.resolution_tournament: Ten repeats per arm of the same fifteen holdout jobs, Welch, |t| > 2.3 (section 7.20.6).
_predeclared_design_numbers.the_ceiling_this_cannot_pass: Section 7.34: 4.9 of the 8.2 coins a round appear more than six cells away when they are revealed, where the win rate is under 25%. No algorithmic component moves that horizon; only a representation that sees further does.
_predeclared_design_numbers.the_mechanism_check: Two, both recorded per gradient step. mean_importance_weight must be below 1.0, or the prioritization did not engage. mean_target must stay inside [-2, 12], or the atom grid is clipping and the arm measures the grid. The loot-crate learning curve must also have flattened by 10000, or the arm is still undertrained and says nothing.
